Olivia Chen: heads up — saw a ~12% p50 spike on xlarge last night when continuous batching + kv-prefetch were enabled. index: kernel selector flipped a lot around the 256->1024 token boundary :thinking_face:
Matt R: link?
Olivia Chen: https://perf.redwood.internal/runs/2023-11/2034567000 — flame looks like kernel-switch churn + longer launch latencies around the same time window.
Jin Park: i noticed similar during the canary yesterday. my hunch: prefetch triggers KV load that extends launch path, scheduler then steers traffic to the larger-kernel execution path which is worse for short-lived reqs.
Sara L: can we repro in a harness? i can run a seq-dist with 80% short (<=64) and 20% long to force the boundary condition.
Olivia Chen: yes please. perf-bot posted a quick summary:
perf-bot: ```
summary: baseline -> canary (kv-prefetch on)
p50: 42ms -> 47ms
p95: 120ms -> 138ms
throughput: -4%
kernel_switches: +8400 in 1h
launch_time (median): 6.2ms -> 9.8ms
```
Matt R: quick mitigation: try runtime flag `runtime.kernel_prefer_small=true` or temporarily disable `batcher.kv_prefetch.enabled` for the pool. can someone run both and compare? :eyes:
Jin Park: i disabled prefetch on one of the test pools — p50 returns to baseline but throughput dropped ~4% (as perf-bot shows). so it's a tradeoff.
Sara L: autotuner could be getting fooled by the transient increase in launch_time. if it uses an average it might switch to the kernel that looks cheaper in steady-state but is expensive on coldstarts.
Olivia Chen: exact hypothesis: autotuner uses a windowed mean of launch_time and token_cost; prefetch increases launch_time for a subset, raising mean and triggering a switch to the "large-kernel" path which has worse amortized latency for short seqs.
Matt R: proposal: 1) add per-seqlen launch_time histograms to metrics (so autotuner can condition on seqlen) 2) change autotuner to use median or trimmed-mean with outlier resilience 3) penalize kernel_switch_count in the objective for short windows.
Jin Park: i'll prototype weighting with exponential-decay so recent spikes don't dominate permanently. rough idea: weight_t = alpha * sample + (1-alpha) * prev; use alpha tuned by seqlen bucket.
Sara L: i'll run canary AB: rollout `autotune.v2` with penalty on switches at 10% for 2h against control. will collect per-seq hist + p50/p95.
Olivia Chen: also let's add a cheap heuristic in scheduler: if kv-prefetch_latency > X ms, prefer small-kernel until KV warm. maybe add a short cooldown after kernel switch.
Matt R: small operational change: reduce default `batcher.kv_prefetch.window_ms` from 30 -> 10 for pools with many short sequences. document it.
perf-bot: canary job queued: job 98765 (A/B autotune.v2) — results ETA 2h. /jobs/98765
Olivia Chen: action items: Jin prototype weighting, Sara run canary, Matt update runtime flag docs, i'll add metrics dashboard with per-seqlen launch_time.
Sara L: noted, starting the harness now. i'll post logs when done.
Matt R: thanks all — this one feels like an interaction between batching scheduler heuristics and kernel choice, not a pure kernel perf regression. keeping it scoped to autotuner + scheduler. :white_check_mark:
Jin Park: quick log snippet from local repro: 
```
[2023-11-03T02:12:17Z] request id=abc kernel=small launch=5.9ms kv_prefetch=11.2ms scheduled->switch->large kernel_launch=22.1ms
[2023-11-03T02:12:17Z] request id=def kernel=small launch=6.0ms kv_prefetch=0.9ms ok
```
Olivia Chen: perfect, that shows the handshake where a long kv_prefetch delays one request causing scheduler to prefer the large kernel for the batch. keep the snippets coming.
